messages.subject: Strange error with using se = FALSE in geom_smooth()
parts:
Dear all,

I get a strange error when using se = FALSE in geom_smooth. Even
stranger is that it does not occur when using smaller subsamples of the
dataset. The dataset is attached.

Any ideas?

Best regards,

Thierry

> 0

geom_smooth(se = FALSE)

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Strange error with using se = FALSE in geom_smooth()
parts:
On Jul 26, 3:37 am, "ONKELINX, Thierry" <Thierry.ONKEL...@inbo.be>
wrote:

> Dear all,
>
> I get a strange error when using se = FALSE in geom_smooth. Even
> stranger is that it does not occur when using smaller subsamples of the
> dataset. The dataset is attached.
>
> Any ideas?
>
> Best regards,
>
> Thierry

I have not figured out exactly what is happening, but I've narrowed
down the conditions needed to trigger it, and I have a suggestion for
a temporary workaround until the real problem can be understood.

The conditions needed are:
* data with at least two group
* the first group with 1000 or more cases
* a geom_smooth with se=FALSE

If there is only a single group, it works with or without se=FALSE,
independent of the number of cases.

If the first group (where "first" is defined based on the order of the
levels of the grouping variable) has less than 1000 cases, it works
with or without se=FALSE. I assume the 1000 is significant because
that is the threshold which stat_smooth switches from loess to gam.

Without se=FALSE, any combination of size and order works.

As a workaround, if you add method="loess" to you geom_smooth call, it
should work.

=====Example code:

# create a data.frame that satisfies the criteria for the error to
occur
ex2 <- data.frame(A=c(1:1000,seq(1,1000,length=20)),
B=rnorm(1020),
C=rep(c("a","b"),c(1000,20)))

# has all three elements
ggplot(ex2, aes(x=A, y=B, group=C)) + geom_smooth(se=FALSE)
# Error in class(output[[var]]) <- class(value) :
# cannot set class to "array" unless the dimension attribute has
length > 0

# does not include the se=FALSE
ggplot(ex2, aes(x=A, y=B, group=C)) + geom_smooth()
# works

# rearrange the order of the levels on C so the smaller (<1000 cases)
# group is first;
ggplot(transform(ex2, C=factor(C,levels=c("b","a"))),
aes(x=A, y=B, group=C)) + geom_smooth(se=FALSE)
# works

# take away the grouping completely
ggplot(ex2, aes(x=A, y=B)) + geom_smooth(se=FALSE)
# works

# force the smoothing method to be "loess"
ggplot(ex2, aes(x=A, y=B, group=C)) + geom_smooth(se=FALSE,
method="loess")
# works

# Forced use of gam also triggers the error, even with a smaller data
set
ex3 <- data.frame(A=c(1:20,1:20),
B=rnorm(40),
C=rep(c("a","b"),each=20))

# request gam, using the same formula as default in StatSmooth
$calculate
# when more than 1000 cases
ggplot(ex3, aes(x=A, y=B, group=C)) +
geom_smooth(se=FALSE, method="gam", formula=y~s(x,bs="cs"))
#Error in class(output[[var]]) <- class(value) :
# cannot set class to "array" unless the dimension attribute has
length > 0

# take away the grouping
ggplot(ex3, aes(x=A, y=B)) +
geom_smooth(se=FALSE, method="gam", formula=y~s(x,bs="cs"))
# works, though I am not sure that the formula argument is doing
anything

# or take away the se=FALSE
ggplot(ex3, aes(x=A, y=B, group=C)) +
geom_smooth(method="gam", formula=y~s(x,bs="cs"))
# works, though I am not sure that the formula argument is doing
anything

=====End example code

Given these examples, the criteria could be restated as:
* data with at least two group
* a geom_smooth with se=FALSE
* the first group has its smoothing performed with "gam", either by
direct request or by virtue of having 1000 or more cases and using the
default auto selection of smoother

I'm going to let someone else with a better understanding of the guts
of the code figure out why these particular criteria lead to an error.

messages.subject: Re: Strange error with using se = FALSE in geom_smooth()
parts:
hi,

probably this is a bug in ggplot2:::predictdf.glm

the function should be

function (model, xseq, se, level)
{
pred <- stats::predict(model, newdata = data.frame(x = xseq),
se = se, type = "link")
if (se) {
std <- qnorm(level/2 + 0.5)
data.frame(x = xseq, y = model$family$linkinv(as.vector(pred$fit)),
ymin = model$family$linkinv(as.vector(pred$fit -
std * pred$se)), ymax =
model$family$linkinv(as.vector(pred$fit +
std * pred$se)), se = as.vector(pred$se))
}
else {
# the class of pred is array, so it shoud be coerce to vector
# data.frame(x = xseq, y = model$family$linkinv(pred))
data.frame(x = xseq, y = model$family$linkinv(as.vector(pred)))
}
}

the strange behavior is because StatSmooth choose "loess" as fitting
method when the number of cases < 1000 and without specifying the
method.

possibly this bug will be fixed in the next version of ggplot2.
